```{r}
#| label: prep
library(tidyverse)

base <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/main/data/2026/2026-11-03/"
grambank_languages <- read_csv(paste0(base, "grambank_languages.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
grambank_values    <- read_csv(paste0(base, "grambank_values.csv"),    show_col_types = FALSE)

MIN_FEATURES <- 100   # ignore thinly documented languages
K_NETWORK    <- 5     # each language links to its 5 most similar

# languages worth comparing
langs <- grambank_values |>
  count(language_id, name = "n_features") |>
  inner_join(grambank_languages, by = "language_id") |>
  filter(n_features >= MIN_FEATURES, !is.na(latitude)) |>
  mutate(family_name = replace_na(family_name, "Isolate / unclassified"))
vals <- grambank_values |> filter(language_id %in% langs$language_id)

# similarity for ALL pairs = share of co-coded features with the same answer,
# via two matrix products (one-hot answers -> agreements, presence -> shared)
onehot <- function(df, col) {
  m <- table(factor(df$language_id, levels = langs$language_id), df[[col]])
  matrix(as.numeric(m), nrow(m), dimnames = list(rownames(m), colnames(m)))
}
A <- onehot(vals, "code_id"); P <- onehot(vals, "parameter_id")
shared <- tcrossprod(P)
sim    <- tcrossprod(A) / shared
sim[shared < MIN_FEATURES] <- NA
diag(sim) <- NA

# k-nearest-neighbour network (directed: "B is among A's 5 closest")
knn <- map_dfr(rownames(sim), \(id) {
  s <- sort(sim[id, ], decreasing = TRUE)[seq_len(K_NETWORK)]
  tibble(from = id, to = names(s), sim = unname(s))
}) |> filter(!is.na(sim))

# hub score: how many languages count this one among their 5 closest
hub <- count(knn, language_id = to, name = "hub")

# undirected links for drawing, with both ends' coordinates
coords <- select(langs, language_id, lon = longitude, lat = latitude)
links <- knn |>
  mutate(a = pmin(from, to), b = pmax(from, to)) |>
  distinct(a, b, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  left_join(rename(coords, a = language_id, lon1 = lon, lat1 = lat), by = "a") |>
  left_join(rename(coords, b = language_id, lon2 = lon, lat2 = lat), by = "b") |>
  select(from = a, to = b, lon1, lat1, lon2, lat2, sim)

# family groups for colouring: 8 biggest families + Other
top_fam <- langs |> filter(family_name != "Isolate / unclassified") |>
  count(family_name, sort = TRUE) |> slice_head(n = 8) |> pull(family_name)

# each language's 195 answers as one compact string ("." = not coded),
# so the browser can compute similarity to any language on the fly
params <- sort(unique(grambank_values$parameter_id))
feat <- vals |>
  mutate(parameter_id = factor(parameter_id, params)) |>
  select(language_id, parameter_id, value) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = parameter_id, values_from = value,
              names_expand = TRUE, values_fill = NA) |>
  select(language_id, all_of(params)) |>
  mutate(across(-language_id, \(x) replace_na(as.character(x), "."))) |>
  unite("f", -language_id, sep = "")

nodes <- langs |>
  left_join(hub, by = "language_id") |>
  left_join(feat, by = "language_id") |>
  transmute(id = language_id, name = language_name, family = family_name,
            area = macroarea, lon = longitude, lat = latitude,
            fam = if_else(family_name %in% top_fam, family_name, "Other"),
            hub = replace_na(hub, 0L), f)

ojs_define(nodes = nodes, links = links, fam_domain = c(top_fam, "Other"))
```

Pick a language from the list, or **click any dot on the map**. The map highlights only that language's **10 closest grammatical matches**, numbered from most to least similar and coloured by language family. Switch to **Top 10 hubs** to see the languages that show up most often in other languages' top-5 lists, each joined to its own 5 closest matches.

```{ojs}
//| label: libs
Plot = require("@observablehq/plot@0.6.16")
land = d3.json("https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/world-atlas@2.0.2/land-110m.json")
  .then(w => topojson.feature(w, w.objects.land))
L = transpose(nodes)
E = transpose(links)
byId = new Map(L.map(d => [d.id, d]))
famColours = ["#4E79A7","#F28E2B","#E15759","#76B7B2","#59A14F",
              "#EDC948","#B07AA1","#FF9DA7","#9D9D9D"]
```

```{ojs}
//| label: controls
viewof sel = Inputs.input("hind1269")      // the selected language (shared state)
viewof view = Inputs.radio(["Selected language", "Top 10 hubs"],
                           {value: "Selected language", label: "Show"})
viewof pick = Inputs.bind(
  Inputs.select(
    new Map(L.map(d => [`${d.name} (${d.family})`, d.id])
             .sort((a, b) => a[0].localeCompare(b[0]))),
    {label: "Language", width: 360, disabled: view !== "Selected language"}),
  viewof sel)
viewof k = Inputs.range([5, 25], {step: 1, value: 10, label: "Matches to show",
                                  disabled: view !== "Selected language"})
viewof zoom = Inputs.toggle({label: "Zoom to highlighted", value: true})
viewof showNet = Inputs.toggle({label: "Show full network (busy!)", value: false})
```

```{ojs}
//| label: compute
// similarity of two languages: share of co-coded features with the same answer
similarity = (a, b) => {
  let n = 0, m = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < a.length; i++) {
    if (a[i] !== "." && b[i] !== ".") { n++; if (a[i] === b[i]) m++; }
  }
  return n >= 100 ? m / n : NaN;
}
closest = (lang, n) => L.filter(d => d.id !== lang.id)
  .map(d => ({...d, sim: similarity(lang.f, d.f)}))
  .filter(d => !isNaN(d.sim))
  .sort((a, b) => b.sim - a.sim).slice(0, n)

me = byId.get(sel)
data = L.map(d => ({...d, sim: d.id === sel ? NaN : similarity(me.f, d.f)}))
nbrs = closest(me, k).map((d, i) => ({...d, rank: i + 1}))

// the 10 languages that appear most often in other languages' top 5
hubs = L.slice().sort((a, b) => b.hub - a.hub).slice(0, 10)
  .map((d, i) => ({...d, rank: i + 1}))
// each hub joined to its own 5 closest matches (50 lines, not hundreds)
hubLinks = hubs.flatMap(h => closest(h, 5).map(d =>
  ({lon1: h.lon, lat1: h.lat, lon2: d.lon, lat2: d.lat})))
```

```{ojs}
//| label: map
//| column: page
{
  const isHub = view === "Top 10 hubs";
  const focus = isHub ? hubs : nbrs;
  const sMin = d3.min(nbrs, d => d.sim), sMax = d3.max(nbrs, d => d.sim);
  const zoomPts = isHub ? focus : [me, ...focus];
  const xy = {x: "lon", y: "lat"};

  const W = Math.min(width, 1200);
  const fig = Plot.plot({
    width: W, height: Math.round(W * 0.5),
    style: {fontSize: "12px", background: "transparent"},
    projection: zoom
      ? {type: "equal-earth", inset: 40,
         domain: {type: "MultiPoint", coordinates: zoomPts.map(d => [d.lon, d.lat])}}
      : "equal-earth",
    color: {type: "categorical", domain: fam_domain, range: famColours,
            legend: true, label: "Language family"},
    marks: [
      Plot.sphere({fill: "#E8F0F3", stroke: "#E2DBCD", clip: "frame"}),
      Plot.geo(land, {fill: "#E6DFD2", stroke: "#FFFFFF", strokeWidth: 0.4, clip: "frame"}),
      showNet ? Plot.link(E, {x1: "lon1", y1: "lat1", x2: "lon2", y2: "lat2",
                               stroke: "#333", strokeOpacity: 0.05, strokeWidth: 0.5,
                               clip: "frame"}) : null,
      // every language as a faint grey dot, for context only
      Plot.dot(L, {...xy, r: 1.6, fill: "#A9A59D", fillOpacity: 0.7, clip: "frame"}),
      // the connections
      isHub
        ? Plot.link(hubLinks, {x1: "lon1", y1: "lat1", x2: "lon2", y2: "lat2",
                               stroke: "#0B7A5C", strokeOpacity: 0.6, strokeWidth: 1,
                               clip: "frame"})
        : Plot.link(nbrs, {x1: () => me.lon, y1: () => me.lat, x2: "lon", y2: "lat",
                           stroke: "#0B7A5C", strokeOpacity: 0.8, clip: "frame",
                           strokeWidth: d => 0.8 + 2.5 * (d.sim - sMin) / (sMax - sMin || 1)}),
      // the highlighted languages: coloured by family, numbered by rank
      Plot.dot(focus, {...xy, r: 10, fill: "fam", stroke: "white", strokeWidth: 1.5}),
      Plot.text(focus, {...xy, text: "rank", fill: "white", stroke: "#1b2a3a",
                        strokeWidth: 2.5, fontSize: 11, fontWeight: "bold"}),
      // name the three closest matches (or the three biggest hubs) next to their dots
      Plot.text(focus.filter(d => d.rank <= 3), {...xy, text: "name", dx: 14, textAnchor: "start",
                        fontSize: 12, fontWeight: "bold", fill: "#1b2a3a", stroke: "white", strokeWidth: 4}),
      // the selected language
      isHub ? null : Plot.dot([me], {...xy, r: 10, fill: "#1b2a3a", stroke: "white", strokeWidth: 2.5}),
      isHub ? null : Plot.text([me], {...xy, text: "name", dy: -20, fontSize: 15,
                                      fontWeight: "bold", fill: "#1b2a3a", stroke: "white", strokeWidth: 5}),
      Plot.tip(data, Plot.pointer({
        ...xy,
        title: d => `${d.name}\n${d.family} · ${d.area}\n` +
                    (isHub ? "" : `Similarity to ${me.name}: ${isNaN(d.sim) ? "n/a" : d.sim.toFixed(2)}\n`) +
                    `In the top 5 of ${d.hub} languages\n(click to select)`
      }))
    ]
  });

  // clicking any dot selects that language (and switches to its view)
  fig.addEventListener("click", () => {
    const d = fig.value;
    if (!d) return;
    if (d.id !== sel) {
      viewof sel.value = d.id;
      viewof sel.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", {bubbles: true}));
    }
    if (view !== "Selected language") {
      viewof view.value = "Selected language";
      viewof view.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", {bubbles: true}));
    }
  });
  return fig;
}
```

::: {.grid .column-page}

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
#### Closest matches to the selected language
```{ojs}
//| label: nbr-table
Inputs.table(nbrs.map(d => ({"#": d.rank, Language: d.name, Family: d.family,
                             Similarity: d.sim})),
  {format: {Similarity: x => x.toFixed(3)}, rows: 25, height: 360, layout: "auto"})
```
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
#### Top 10 hubs (most connected languages)
```{ojs}
//| label: hub-table
Inputs.table(hubs.map(d => ({"#": d.rank, Language: d.name, Family: d.family,
                             "In top 5 of": d.hub})),
  {rows: 10, height: 360, layout: "auto"})
```
:::

:::

*Similarity = the share of Grambank features coded for both languages on which they give the same answer (at least 100 shared features required). Hub score = the number of languages that list this one among their 5 closest. Data: Skirgård et al. (2023), Grambank, via TidyTuesday.*
